about: The pack's agent instructions (SNAP-R93): the pack layer of every resolved stack, version 0 of each note. A note has one scope (global, tool:<name>, brick:<key>, method:<id>) and a kind: note (a line an agent reads whole) or model_choice (which model does a job, and why; the person can replace it with their own). tool: notes also ride on that tool's description. rule names the SNAP rule behind it, more where to read further (a skill, AGENT_START, SNAP_RULES); planned names the build that will add its code.

notes.text: Consistency is data, not prompting: carry pictures and state (location master + plates, Cast records with turnarounds, positions cut to cut); words alone make a new place and a new design every render.
Results are never trimmed; if one is too big for your context, save it to a file and hand it to a subagent.
When Snap can't do a job, it is a Snap gap: report what you tried and the tool's answer; a take queued outside Snap never shows in its shot or the Work card.
Warn and explain, never block; marks inform.
Storyboard before video: boards per cut (camera, lens, positions, facing, scale, transition) and an animatic, with cut-pair checks on boards.

When the GPU is idle and the main job waits, start the next useful GPU work toward the goal (the known parts of a fix first), else a cheap experiment that teaches something; record it; never decide what is the person's; run it on the visible page.
Drive the person's main tab or the agents' window; attach to the running window, open it only when nothing answers; never headless.
Another tab needs the person's yes; an extra visible window only for parallel work on another server or GPU, named for its purpose, closed after; never a duplicate of the same page.
After a server restart, reload the agents' window yourself (chrome reload); ask the person with request_reload for their tab.
Lead overall_soundscape with the discrete sounds the action makes, ambience last; an ambience-only soundscape renders near-silent (~-57 dB).
Tonal words (horn, buzz, hum) become drones; use percussive events unless the tone is the point, and confirm a drone with a spectrum, not loudness.
Palette words in the style line get painted onto props; keep them out of shots where a light stays off, and state off states literally.
Never cite the next place on a path as a reference: H3 hard-cut to it in 3 of 8 takes. Cite the cut's own plate, the master and the Cast.

notes.job: a cut whose first frame is the point (a wide, a light igniting in place)
notes.why: copies the still exactly (identity, framing) but invents the set as the camera moves

notes.choice: Ref2V with the plate and Cast pictures
notes.why: holds the plate's set and draws the character from the sheets; ignores a First frame left over from FL2V

notes.text: A known place's new view is made from context pictures (master, nearest prior view, Cast), never words alone.
What Picture 1 is depends on the model (picture_one); for both H3 models the words set the camera.
Pass width and height: ph3_view with 0 makes Picture 1's own size, so a crop gives a small odd still. Board frames at 2-4 MP.
A targeted edit names only the change, its shape, what it is not, and what holds ('her head stays in profile'); without the last part 5/6 turned the head.
A wide from inside a place pulls back to the master's aerial (6/6) unless something at head height anchors the foreground.
Callouts come from a crop ({cast, crop}: 29/30), not from words (0/24).
Land each cut's board in that cut's shot (land).

notes.job: sets, wide shots and targeted edits
notes.why: moves the camera from words (6/6 into the square with the master's own gate), ~7 s a still at 8 steps; its no-change floor is SSIM 0.94-0.96

notes.job: character shots, two-shots and finished board frames
notes.why: closest two-shots; every picture is a reference, so it draws back views (6/6); soft under 2-3 MP; an edit with it re-renders the whole picture

notes.job: a new view of a place
notes.choice: an H3 still model, not MOSS Image Edit
notes.why: MOSS edit copied Picture 1 or redesigned the set and the people across views

notes.job: a board still bigger than 4 MP
notes.why: ~5 s; the H3 latent refine is softer and 7x slower

notes.text: Build a location as set plan + master + one people-free forward-dolly walkthrough; pull plates from its frames with their camera pose.
Forward dollies hold a set; turns snap back to the master's pose (4/4).
Plate prompts describe the place only ('no figures'); say what is not there; keep establishing plates people-free; put seats and anchors in the plate.
Cite plates by take frame (use_take {take, as: reference, at}) instead of exporting files.
A back view needs a back reference: from a front picture alone back views mirrored the carried prop 6/6.
Measure the reference's shape first: a portrait picture rolls the five-view LoRA's camera (4/6); padded square it orbits 9/9.
Check what holds every carried object (strap, sheath, belt, hand) in every view before the sheet becomes a Cast picture.
'Seen from above' never appears in a one-sheet turnaround (0/6).
Keep sheets neutral; acting (goggles down, eyes opening) goes in the video prompt.

notes.choice: one continuous H3 orbit (an orbit LoRA such as ORB360 on Ref2VA, front + back pictures, 20 steps), frames at 90/180/270
notes.why: one video keeps carried objects consistent by construction; passed every per-view check where stills guessed each side

notes.job: a turnaround without an orbit LoRA
notes.why: Picture 1 padded square orbits front to back 9/9, ~39 s a sheet
kept a scabbard on the back in profile 5/6

notes.job: a sheet that must keep carried props
notes.choice: not krea2_quadview (drops props) or moss_charref (off-model); krea2_dynamic only for pitch sheets (garbled labels)

notes.text: Keep a single-figure front view as the Cast's first picture: a three-view sheet made a recast paint three people.
A Cast state's picture decides expression; a new look needs a new picture, not only words.
Before saying a look changed, look at the take (take_frames): a version number says what Snap put in, not what the model drew.
Recast: give who a short description of the person to replace, not the old Cast's details line (that added the new person beside the old).
Ripple (relight, Change something) re-renders the sound; Remake keeps it.

notes.job: Change something on a video take
notes.choice: MOSS Image Edit paints the frames, then H3 Ripple / Viggle Remake
notes.why: the in-place video edit route; MOSS left only New view

notes.choice: Standard up to ~40 s, Long beyond; Strong only as a pick
notes.why: Standard grows a mosaic past ~40 s; Long's re-anchor holds 2 minutes, face and sound

notes.text: A drone in an extended take is usually the prompt's tonal words, not the carry: Long stayed clean for 34 s once they left.
Measure long-clip drift with a looping prompt so same-phase segments compare like for like.
Look at whole frames at several angles before face crops: a tiled upscale grew ghost figures in its backdrop while the face looked great.
A 2K stage 2 pass at cfg 5 fills a 32 GB card (~2.5 min a step); Tessera's 4K decode writes ~10 GB to TESSERA_SCRATCH.

notes.job: making a reference bigger (Cast picture, turnaround, plate, settei)
notes.why: redraws the smeared face: ArcFace vs the Cast front 0.91/0.86/0.89 vs 0.79/0.68/0.80 for sharpen-only RelayVSR

notes.text: stage2 speed "fast" (cfg 1) is about 1.7x faster and a touch softer; quality stays the default. Offer fast for drafts or when the person asks; for a final reference pick, make both and let the person choose.

notes.choice: tessera after stage2 (anchored on its frame 0, flat_skip 8)
notes.why: carries the redrawn face up; on its own its backdrop tiles grew ghost copies

notes.text: A voice note of check means listen: two similar voices overlap in WavLM (two young women 0.81-0.95, the same speaker 0.89-1.00). Read the margin and the F0 against the reference before recasting.
Make a voice reference at 12 steps or more, low resolution is fine; ordinary takes stay at the setup's steps.
Text alone doesn't cast a voice (pitch, age and sex words are ignored): anchor it with a talking take and cite <Audio n> in every cut where the character speaks.
Measure a voice before calling it cast: the Voice QA's words and who said each line (check_voice, SNAP-R240), F0 median and range, speaker similarity against the reference.
Audio uploads with subfolder=snap; Load Audio lists input/snap/.
Whole frame at full resolution first, crops second.
Check logic, not only consistency: enclosures close, roads reach gates, what holds each carried object; contact, attachments, intersections.
Judge masters, sheets and plates too; compare every view of a location side by side and against its master; put the previous cut's last frame beside each cut.
Fix a flaw at its source record and re-run its dependents; a new seed keeps a plate's flaw.
State the baseline before reading a face score: a bowed profile scores 0.06 and relighting 0.34-0.60; the head crops decide.
A mark is a visible mask with its note; 'Fix this' uses the mask as the edit region or routes to the source record.
Each file needs the person's yes; safetensors only.
Read a pack's code per the person's code-review setting, and grep installed packs for its node ids first.
A third-party character catalog is linked, never shipped or offered as Cast sources.
Never poll JSON files or sleep: wait_for answers; quote times as first seed / each more seed, from /history.
Read every whole frame before any tile, then the context pictures; read the checklist's section of the snap-critic skill's reference.md.
The owner is where the flaw was born: a flaw already in the master or a plate is theirs even when you see it in a board. A clean verdict with no notes is a valid answer.
Fix the source record first (a new master or plate version), then re-run its dependents; the chain stops before video unless through: cuts.
